question.text: Suppose a uniformly charged wall provides a uniform electric field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> normally. A charged particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> being suspended through a silk thread of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and remain stayed at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the wall. Then the charge on the particle will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></math> ________ [use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
As we can see from geometry, sinθ=1020=12

⇒θ=30°

Vertical component of tension will balance the weight and the horizontal component will balance the electric force. Therefore,

tanθ=qEmg

⇒tan30°=q×2×1042×10-3×10

⇒13=q×106

⇒q=13×10-6 C=13 μC

Hence, x=3.
